PUBLIC RESPONSE: f4, g4

The only moves that force a win in the minimum number of moves are the double-threat setups on the 4th rank.

f4 completes d4-O e4-O f4-O. From here O threatens both c4 to make c4-d4-e4-f4 and g4 to make d4-e4-f4-g4. X can only block one of c4 or g4 on the next move, so O wins immediately on the following move. The diagonal c6-d5-e4 is also kept alive because the f-file stays open.

g4 is the defensive-offensive move. It blocks X’s vertical three-in-a-row on g6-g5-g4 and simultaneously creates the same d-e-f-g four-in-a-row threat: after g4, f4 wins d4-e4-f4-g4. If X tries to block f4, the diagonal c6-d5-e4-f3 is now reachable on the f-file and O wins on the diagonal. c4 only creates a single horizontal three c4-d4-e4 and does not force the same immediate double-threat, so it is slower under optimal defence.

O already has d4 and e4 on the 4th rank from the top. The fastest forced win is to make a three-in-a-row with two open ends on that rank.

c4 gives O on c4 d4 e4. The four is then completed on either b4 or f4 on the next move, so X can block only one of the two winning squares. The same double threat is obtained with f4, which gives d4 e4 f4 and is completed on the next move by c4 or g4.

g4 only gives d4 e4 g4 with the single immediate continuation f4. After g4 X can block f4 and the win is delayed, so g4 is not a fastest forced win, whereas c4 and f4 both force a win on O’s next move regardless of X’s defence.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: c4, d4, f4

The fourth rank is the decisive rank. O already owns e4 and f4 in the matrix view, so the e-f pair is the core of the forced win. Playing d4 completes the d e f three-in-a-row on that rank and forces an immediate block from X; the same three is the mirror of the e f g threat that O is building on the right side of the board. 

c4 is the other fast-forcing square. From c4 O gets the up-right diagonal c4-d5-e6 with d5 already O, and it also supports the c-d-e horizontal build on the third playable line. With c in place X cannot cover both the d e f horizontal and the c-d-e diagonal threat at once.

f4 is the central reinforcement. It sustains the e-f pair, keeps the e-f-g horizontal alive for the next move and denies X the chance to drop a piece underneath the e-f block. Together c4, d4 and f4 give O a two-pronged forced win on the fourth rank and the c-d-e diagonal, and they are the fastest forcing continuations in the position.
